cases.title: Building a data architecture platform.
cases.context: Flexilant Works · Client: SIX Swiss Exchange
cases.description: Helped architect and build a platform on OpenShift Kubernetes, integrating orchestration, query, storage and workflow services within enterprise access controls.

contributions.title: Architecture & integration
contributions.description: Helped architect and build a data architecture platform; deployed and integrated Airflow, Trino, MinIO, Metaflow, Argo Workflows and Argo Events.

contributions.title: Deployment within controls
contributions.description: Used Helm for service configuration and ArgoCD for application delivery. Adapted releases to namespace RBAC, service accounts, approved registries and controlled networking.

contributions.title: Airflow end to end
contributions.description: Deployed Apache Airflow end to end, authored DAGs, and implemented workflow monitoring with Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager and Elasticsearch.

contributions.title: Application dependencies
contributions.description: Worked with Kubeseal and Kubernetes Sealed Secrets. Investigated dependencies across secrets, persistent volumes, PostgreSQL connectivity, DNS and TLS.

cases.decision: A Helm chart is only part of a deployment. Application dependencies, permissions, registry access and network reachability all have to fit the target environment.
cases.scope: These notes describe my contributions through Flexilant Works. The diagram is a conceptual grouping of technologies, not SIX Swiss Exchange’s internal topology.
cases.constraints: Restricted namespaces, service-account permissions, approved registries, sealed secrets and controlled network paths shaped how services could be deployed and integrated.
cases.delivered: Contributed platform architecture and integration, Helm-based deployments and ArgoCD delivery, with Airflow DAGs and workflow monitoring.

cases.title: A standard path from code to delivery.
cases.description: Migrated a frontend GitLab CI pipeline to an organisational golden path. Designed a separate deployment pipeline for a Python/FastAPI backend.

contributions.title: Frontend migration — implemented
contributions.description: Migrated one frontend application’s custom GitLab CI pipeline to an organisation-standard golden-path component.

contributions.title: Standard quality jobs — adopted
contributions.description: Adopted the component’s build, lint, test, audit and SonarQube jobs rather than maintaining an application-specific pipeline implementation.

contributions.title: Backend pipeline — designed
contributions.description: Designed a GitLab CI deployment pipeline for a Python/FastAPI backend.

contributions.title: Deployment approaches — evaluated
contributions.description: Evaluated SSH push-based deployment against the organisation’s Ansible deployment approach.

cases.decision: The frontend migration was implemented. The backend work involved pipeline design and comparison of deployment approaches; these are distinct contributions.
cases.scope: The comparison shows the verified frontend standardisation concept. It makes no claim about deployment speed, defect reduction or adoption across other teams.
cases.constraints: The frontend needed to use the organisation-standard pipeline component. Backend deployment was a separate design problem with an established Ansible approach to consider.
cases.delivered: Completed the frontend migration to the golden-path component. Produced a separate Python/FastAPI deployment design and evaluated SSH versus Ansible; no backend implementation or speed improvement is implied.

cases.title: Reliability spans more than the workload.
cases.description: Worked across production RKE infrastructure with 200+ worker nodes and 10PB+ of Rook-Ceph storage. Investigated failures across compute, networking and storage dependencies.

contributions.title: Production Kubernetes
contributions.description: Worked on production RKE Kubernetes infrastructure with 200+ worker nodes, including deployments, service routing, networking and persistent storage.

contributions.title: Distributed storage recovery
contributions.description: Operated 10PB+ of Rook-Ceph block, file and object storage, alongside MinIO. Diagnosed Ceph/OSD failures, recovered affected components and checked dependent workloads.

contributions.title: Infrastructure & application changes
contributions.description: Applied infrastructure changes with Terraform and Ansible, and delivered application changes with Helm and ArgoCD.

contributions.title: Visibility & automation
contributions.description: Worked on Prometheus, Grafana and Alertmanager for Kubernetes/Linux visibility; maintained Jenkins and GitLab CI pipelines and developed Python and Bash automation.

cases.decision: Investigate the dependency, not just the symptom. A workload issue can involve resource pressure, scheduling, networking, persistent volumes or the underlying storage system.
cases.scope: Scale figures belong to NPCI only. They describe environments I worked on, not sole ownership, a payment transaction-processing topology or an availability guarantee.
cases.constraints: Workload health depended on compute, scheduling, networking and persistent storage. Investigation had to follow the affected dependencies across those layers.
cases.delivered: Delivered infrastructure and application changes, monitoring and automation, and recovery of affected storage components with checks on dependent workloads. The diagram illustrates an investigation approach, not a particular incident record.

delivery.label: Delivery
delivery.title: A commit is the beginning.
delivery.description: Follow the responsibilities between source, validation, configuration and deployment.

nodes.title: Source
nodes.subtitle: Git repository
nodes.detail: Application code and deployment configuration begin as versioned changes. Source control records what is proposed and what can be reviewed.
nodes.connection: The CI pipeline runs against a particular source revision.

nodes.title: Validate
nodes.subtitle: GitLab CI
nodes.detail: The frontend golden path supplies build, lint, test, audit and SonarQube jobs through a shared component.
nodes.connection: Validation and build outputs prepare a change for delivery. Exact jobs depend on the application.

nodes.title: Package
nodes.subtitle: Build output
nodes.detail: In this educational flow, a build produces a deployable artifact or image. This step explains the pattern; it does not assert a specific employer registry layout.
nodes.connection: Approved build inputs and configuration are needed by the deployment process.

nodes.title: Configure
nodes.subtitle: Helm + ArgoCD
nodes.detail: Helm expresses application configuration. ArgoCD delivers application changes through the established GitOps platform, subject to its repository and access controls.
nodes.connection: Rendered resources must fit namespace permissions and platform prerequisites.

nodes.title: Deploy
nodes.subtitle: Kubernetes
nodes.detail: Inspect readiness, resources, secrets, storage and service connectivity. A successful pipeline job alone does not establish that an application is working.
nodes.connection: Workload behaviour is then inspected through metrics, logs and application checks.

platform.label: Platform
platform.title: Services become a platform together.
platform.description: Inspect the boundaries between orchestration, applications and the dependencies they need.

nodes.title: Access
nodes.subtitle: RBAC + registries
nodes.detail: Restricted enterprise namespaces shape deployment choices: service accounts, namespace RBAC, approved images and controlled network access have to be accounted for.
nodes.connection: A chart must use resources and privileges available in the target namespace.

nodes.title: Release
nodes.subtitle: Helm + GitOps
nodes.detail: Configure Helm releases for the platform and deliver application changes through ArgoCD. Centrally managed services remain subject to their existing governance.
nodes.connection: Configuration determines how services reach their dependencies.

nodes.title: Services
nodes.subtitle: Workflows + query
nodes.detail: My platform work includes Airflow, Trino, Metaflow, Argo Workflows and Argo Events. This grouping shows areas of work, not a claim that every service directly calls every other service.
nodes.connection: Workloads need appropriate connectivity, storage and credentials.

nodes.title: Dependencies
nodes.subtitle: Data + connectivity
nodes.detail: Persistent volumes, MinIO object storage, PostgreSQL connectivity, DNS and TLS are part of the deployment and troubleshooting context.
nodes.connection: Check the specific failing dependency rather than assuming application code is at fault.

nodes.title: Secrets
nodes.subtitle: Controlled configuration
nodes.detail: Work with service accounts, secrets, Kubeseal and Kubernetes Sealed Secrets without exposing sensitive configuration.
nodes.connection: Secret references, access and application configuration must agree.

reliability.label: Reliability
reliability.title: Symptoms travel across layers.
reliability.description: Explore illustrative investigation signals. There is no live cluster or production telemetry connected.

nodes.title: Workload
nodes.subtitle: Readiness + failures
nodes.detail: Illustrative checks: pod status, restart history, readiness and recent changes. Establish which workloads and dependencies are affected.
nodes.connection: Workload symptoms guide the next set of infrastructure checks.

nodes.title: Metrics
nodes.subtitle: Prometheus + Grafana
nodes.detail: Illustrative signals include CPU and memory pressure, node conditions, persistent-volume status and storage health. No numerical values here represent a real environment.
nodes.connection: Correlate resource behaviour with events and logs.

nodes.title: Logs
nodes.subtitle: Elasticsearch
nodes.detail: Logs and events can reveal connectivity errors, TLS problems, missing configuration or a failing application dependency.
nodes.connection: Compare logs with the affected workload’s dependencies.

nodes.title: Investigate
nodes.subtitle: Compute / network / storage
nodes.detail: For storage incidents, inspect Ceph/OSD health, identify affected volumes and workloads, and recover failed components. Other investigations may involve DNS, TLS or scheduling.
nodes.connection: The recovery action should address the identified failure.

nodes.title: Verify
nodes.subtitle: Recovery + alerts
nodes.detail: Recheck storage health, affected pods and application dependencies after recovery. Monitoring and Alertmanager provide continuing operational visibility.
nodes.connection: Recovery is checked at the dependent workload as well as the recovered component.

capabilities.name: Platform integration
capabilities.line: Make services work within the platform’s boundaries.
capabilities.tools: Deployment: OpenShift Kubernetes, Helm, ArgoCD. Integration: Airflow, Trino, MinIO, Metaflow and Argo Workflows/Events.
capabilities.example: Deployed and integrated data-platform services under restricted namespace, registry and network access.

capabilities.name: Delivery & automation
capabilities.line: Turn application changes into reviewable delivery workflows.
capabilities.tools: Pipeline components: GitLab CI, Jenkins. Provisioning and configuration: Terraform, Ansible. Automation: Python, Bash.
capabilities.example: Migrated a frontend pipeline to standard components and designed deployment for a Python/FastAPI backend.

capabilities.name: Observability & reliability
capabilities.line: Connect workload symptoms to infrastructure evidence.
capabilities.tools: Signals: Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager, Elasticsearch. Infrastructure investigation: Linux, Rook-Ceph.
capabilities.example: Worked across Kubernetes/Linux monitoring and Ceph/OSD failure investigation at NPCI.

capabilities.name: Security & governance
capabilities.line: Design deployments around real access controls.
capabilities.tools: RBAC, service accounts, private registries, Kubeseal, Sealed Secrets, DNS, TLS
capabilities.example: Adapted Helm releases to controlled enterprise namespaces without assuming cluster-administrator access.

capabilities.name: Cloud & systems
capabilities.line: Work across hosts, cloud services and application dependencies.
capabilities.tools: AWS EC2, S3, IAM, VPC, CloudWatch; Linux; Python; Bash; Terraform; Ansible
capabilities.example: Used AWS alongside on-premises infrastructure, with infrastructure provisioning and host configuration automation.

capabilities.name: AI-assisted engineering
capabilities.line: Use coding agents as part of an accountable development workflow.
capabilities.tools: Cursor, Claude, GitHub Copilot, coding agents, reusable agent skills
capabilities.example: Extensive hands-on use for engineering changes, including deployment configuration, CI/CD and automation. Changes are reviewed and tested before use.

journey.summary: SIX Swiss Exchange engagement. Platform architecture, integration, deployment and delivery automation with an international engineering team.
Production RKE Kubernetes, distributed storage, infrastructure changes and failure investigation.
Kubernetes/Linux observability, Jenkins and GitLab CI pipelines, Helm, AWS, Python and Bash.
Pre-production Kubernetes, Docker builds and deployments, MinIO and initial Rook-Ceph setup.
